project: Des Moines AI Pulse — Web Platform Autonomy & Core Uplift
description: Deep uplift of the WEB platform across Security, Autonomy, Performance, UX, and Features. The governing theme: the site should run itself — content ingestion, data quality, moderation, publishing, marketing, and ops must not require manual admin touches; humans only handle escalated exceptions. Clusters in priority order: (1) WEB-SEC: close the publicly-callable/cost-abusable edge function holes and harden authz before adding more automation on top of them; (2) WEB-AUTO: build the autonomy control plane (job observability) then convert every manual admin queue (event submissions, data backfills, broken links, dedupe, stale content, articles, newsletters, moderation, creative approval, sitemaps, social, subscription lifecycle) into a self-running pipeline with AI scoring + human-exception escalation; (3) WEB-PERF: query payload + bundle + re-render fixes toward the <500KB / LCP<2.5s budgets; (4) WEB-UX: list-page state, loading/error consistency, a11y; (5) WEB-FEAT: web parity with shipped iOS monetization (contextual paywalls, annual+trial, ads/sponsored) plus engagement loops (saved searches+alerts, guest favorites, personalization). CONSTRAINTS THAT BIND EVERY STORY: follow CLAUDE.md backward-compatibility rules — live iOS/Android binaries call edge functions (get_active_ads, discover-chat, generate-itinerary, image-transform, validate-*-receipt, etc.), so NEVER tighten validation, rename/remove endpoints or fields, or lower rate limits below what shipped clients retry against in a single release; DB changes additive-only per the deprecation flow; console logs wrapped in import.meta.env.DEV; storage via @/lib/safeStorage; errors via @/lib/errorHandler. Ralph picks the highest-priority story with passes:false.

Per-user monthly quota checks for tiered AI features are enforced server-side (free/insider/vip limits matching useSubscription web copy), returning 429 with a structured body the web client surfaces as an upgrade prompt

BACKWARD COMPAT: limits are set at-or-above what shipped iOS binaries can legitimately hit (CLAUDE.md forbids tightening below what old clients retry against); response shapes for existing 200 paths unchanged

BACKWARD COMPAT: all limits kept at prior values (10/15min burst, 30/15min chat) so older iOS clients are unaffected; no 200-path response shapes changed. userStories.notes: DONE (2026-06-12): scripts/audit-rls.ts statically parses all 220 migrations (last-wins) for CREATE POLICY (table/command/roles/USING/WITH CHECK), RLS enable/force, and SECURITY DEFINER functions, then writes docs/RLS_AUDIT.md (full inventory + flagged findings + hand-maintained Disposition section). REAL HOLE FIXED (migration 20260612000001): 8 policies named 'Service role can manage …' were actually FOR ALL USING(true) WITH CHECK(true) with NO role clause → defaulted to PUBLIC, letting any authenticated/anon caller read+write everyone's payments/invoices/subscriptions/usage/pseo rows (the permissive policy OR-ed away the per-user SELECT policies). Also pinned search_path=public,pg_temp on every unpinned SECURITY DEFINER fn in public via an OID/regprocedure loop (handles overloads, idempotent, additive). userStories.title: Automated brute-force login detection and temporary lockout
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I need failed-login abuse handled automatically: the login_attempts table exists (migration 20260402000002) but nothing watches it, so credential-stuffing runs unimpeded.
acceptanceCriteria: Auth failure path records to login_attempts (ip, email, timestamp, success=false) via an edge function or existing hook — verify what already writes it and complete the wiring
A check at login time blocks (returns a 'try again later' state) when >5 failures from one IP or >10 for one email within 10 minutes; lockout expires automatically after 15 minutes
Lockout events are logged to security_audit_logs; the affected user gets a notification email (via existing Resend/SendGrid plumbing) on email-keyed lockouts
False-positive safety: successful login resets the counter; lockout never applies to a request presenting a valid existing session
Web login form surfaces the lockout state with a clear, non-enumerating message (same message whether or not the account exists)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: DONE (2026-06-12): login_attempts truly had no consumer — check-login-attempt existed but was called by NOTHING in src/ (web used only a bypassable in-memory Map throttle in AuthContext). Wired the server-side function into AuthContext.login: pre-auth 'check' (blocks with the server message), 'record_failure' on auth error, 'record_success' on success (resets counter). New checkServerLockout() helper FAILS OPEN (returns null) on any error so an outage never blocks sign-in. Enhanced check-login-attempt: now locks on >10 failures for one EMAIL or >5 from one IP within a 10-min window (added IP-keyed counting via the existing client_ip column), lockout lasts 15 min; hardened IP extraction (CF-Connecting-IP, never the spoofable leftmost XFF); fail-open on DB error preserved. On the transition INTO lockout it writes a security_audit_logs row (event_type=account_lockout) and sends a best-effort notification email to the account owner via Resend + shared renderEmail — ONLY when a profile exists for the email (non-enumerating, no spam to random addresses; IP-only lockouts notify no one). Message is identical regardless of whether the account exists or which signal tripped (non-enumerating); Auth.tsx surfaces it via the existing toast. Valid-session requests never hit this path (login() is unauthenticated-only). Verified: type-check passes; edge fn parses via esbuild; AuthContext lints 0 errors. Evidence was: migration 20260402000002 + no caller.

acceptanceCriteria: Audit which entry chunks contain three.js/recharts/leaflet/fullcalendar (npm run build:analyze before/after, numbers in progress notes); none of them load on first paint of / for a cold visit
Homepage hero (EnhancedHero / HeroCityLite in src/pages/Index.tsx) renders a static fallback immediately and upgrades to the 3D scene via dynamic import on idle/intersection; mobile can stay static
Detail-page maps lazy-load on scroll-into-view with a placeholder (location text + 'View map') — applies to Event/Restaurant/Attraction details
Charts (admin/analytics pages) and calendar views load via lazy() route-level splitting only
Lighthouse or Playwright perf spec shows improved LCP/TTI on / (record numbers); no CLS regression from fallback swaps
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: vite.config.ts already has manualChunks + a removeLazyPreloads transform — verify what it actually strips before changing it; the perf agent suspected modulepreload still pulls vendor chunks early.

userStories.title: Image CLS elimination + right-sized responsive images
userStories.description: As a user on a slow connection, I need pages not to jump as images arrive, and thumbnails to download at thumbnail size.
acceptanceCriteria: Every list-card and detail-hero image renders inside a fixed aspect-ratio container (or explicit width/height) — no layout shift on load; CLS < 0.1 on /, /events, /restaurants and one detail page (measure and record)
OptimizedImage gains srcset/sizes using the image-transform width param so cards fetch card-sized images; hero fetches ~viewport width
Dialog/modal images (e.g. event quick-view in src/pages/Index.tsx ~797-807) don't prefetch while the dialog is closed
Fallback path verified: a failed transform falls back to the original URL (never a broken image)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Pairs with WEB-SEC-007's image-transform caching. iOS prd POLISH-002 notes document the image-transform contract (verify_jwt=false, ?url=&width=&quality=) — reuse that knowledge.

userStories.title: Split AuthContext to stop app-wide re-renders
userStories.description: As a user, I need navigation to stay smooth: AuthContext currently carries one object with ~7 fields, so any auth tick re-renders every useAuth() consumer (header, nav, gates — 50+ components).
acceptanceCriteria: AuthContext split into state and actions contexts (or equivalent memoized selector pattern) so login/logout function identities are stable and consumers re-render only when fields they read change
useAuth() keeps its existing public API (zero call-site churn) — implemented as a composition of the new contexts
React DevTools profile (or a render-count test) demonstrates Header/BottomNav no longer re-render on session refresh ticks; numbers in progress notes
All Playwright auth-related flows pass locally (login, protected routes, premium gates)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Evidence: src/contexts/AuthContext.tsx ~87-96. Keep the change mechanical and well-tested — this file is load-bearing for every protected surface.

userStories.title: TanStack Query cache + retry tuning per data class
userStories.description: As a returning visitor, I need instant back-navigation and resilient fetches on flaky networks: one-size-fits-all gcTime/retry currently forces refetches and gives up too fast.
acceptanceCriteria: QueryClient defaults (src/main.tsx) tuned: public content lists get staleTime 5-15min + gcTime 30min; user-specific data keeps short staleTime; documented constants, not magic numbers
retry becomes a function: up to 2 retries with backoff for network/5xx, never for 401/403/404
Back-navigation to a recently-visited list renders from cache instantly (verify manually, note in progress)
No staleness bugs introduced on user-mutated data (favorites, reviews use invalidation correctly — spot-check the mutation hooks)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Evidence: src/main.tsx ~161-164 (retry: 1, gcTime 5min global).

userStories.title: Real-user web-vitals monitoring with automated regression alerts
userStories.description: As the platform owner, I want performance regressions to report themselves: add RUM web-vitals collection and an automated weekly check, so a bad deploy is caught by machines, not complaints.
acceptanceCriteria: web-vitals library reports LCP/CLS/INP/TTFB from real sessions to a Supabase table (sampled, anonymous, additive schema; respect DNT)

A weekly scheduled job (WEB-AUTO-001 jobRunner) computes p75 per metric per page-group, compares against the previous week, and alerts (email) if any metric degrades > 20% or breaches budget (LCP 2.5s, CLS 0.1, INP 200ms)
Admin dashboard panel renders the trend (reuse existing charting, lazy-loaded)
Collection adds < 3KB to the bundle and never blocks rendering (dynamic import on idle)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Autonomy-themed perf: closes the loop so the perf stories above stay won. No web-vitals reporting exists today per the audit.

userStories.title: URL-synced filter state on Events/Restaurants/Attractions
userStories.description: As a user, I want my filtered view to survive back-navigation and be shareable: filters today are component state only, so back loses everything and links can't carry a filter.
acceptanceCriteria: Search text, category/cuisine, date presets, sort, and page sync to URL search params (useSearchParams) on Events, Restaurants, Attractions list pages — debounced so typing doesn't spam history
Loading a URL with params applies all filters on mount; back/forward restores prior filter states; Clear-all resets the URL
Navigating to a detail and back restores the filtered list (URL is the source of truth, replacing any sessionStorage hacks)
SEO landing routes (/events/today etc.) keep working and compose with extra params
Playwright search-filters suite extended with a back-button + shareable-URL test; suite passes
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Top UX-audit finding. Evidence: src/pages/EventsPage.tsx ~102-116, src/pages/Restaurants.tsx ~85-95 (pure useState filters).

userStories.title: Unified loading/empty/error states with retry across all list pages
userStories.description: As a user, I should always know whether the page is loading, empty, or broken — and be able to retry — instead of mixed skeletons, missing empty states, and silent failures per page.
acceptanceCriteria: All content list pages (Events, Restaurants, Attractions, Articles, Deals, Hotels) use the shared skeleton components shape-matched to their real cards while loading (no generic spinners), the shared EmptyState (icon + copy + Clear-filters/Browse CTA) when zero results, and a shared error card with a working Retry button (query refetch) on failure
Skeletons respect prefers-reduced-motion
Error copy distinguishes offline vs server error where detectable
Zero-result state differs between 'no content at all' and 'no matches for your filters'
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Evidence: src/components/ui/loading-skeleton.tsx + empty-state.tsx exist but adoption is inconsistent (EventsPage lacks EmptyState; error handling diverges per page).

userStories.title: Sticky search bar, persistent filter chips, and visible result counts (mobile-first)
userStories.description: As a mobile user filtering a long list, I need to see my active filters and the match count without scrolling back up or reopening a sheet.
acceptanceCriteria: Events/Restaurants/Attractions: search + filter trigger stick below the header on scroll (no layout shift when sticking)
Active filters render as removable chips above results with a 'Clear all'; chips visible at all viewports
Result count ('N results') visible on mobile (currently hidden md:block on Restaurants) and announced via aria-live
Closing the mobile filter sheet returns focus to the trigger button (a11y)
Playwright mobile-responsive suite covers the sticky bar + chips; suite passes
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Evidence: result count hidden on mobile (src/pages/Restaurants.tsx ~503); filters live in the hero so they scroll away. Mirrors what IOS-IA-004 shipped natively.

userStories.title: Detail-page upgrades: related rail, last-updated badge, named breadcrumbs
userStories.description: As a user on an event/restaurant/attraction detail page, I want obvious next steps (related content), trust signals (data freshness), and sane breadcrumbs (names, not UUIDs).
acceptanceCriteria: Event/Restaurant/Attraction detail pages render a 'More like this' rail (3-4 cards, same category/area) placed after the primary content — Restaurants already queries relatedRestaurants but never renders it; rail hidden when < 3 matches
'Updated X ago' badge near the title using updated_at (full timestamp on hover/tap)
Breadcrumbs show the item name on dynamic routes instead of the raw id (src/components/ui/breadcrumbs.tsx accepts a label override)
Related-rail clicks tracked so engagement lift is measurable
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Evidence: RestaurantDetails fetches related but doesn't render; breadcrumbs.tsx ~35-54 derives labels from the pathname.

userStories.title: Keyboard accessibility pass: autocomplete, card actions, focus management
userStories.description: As a keyboard/screen-reader user, I need search suggestions, card secondary actions, and sheet/dialog flows to be fully operable.
acceptanceCriteria: SearchAutocomplete supports ArrowUp/Down + Enter + Escape with aria-activedescendant and announced selection
Card secondary actions (favorite, share) are tabbable with explicit aria-labels ('Save {name}'), reachable without entering the card link
Sheets/dialogs restore focus to their trigger on close across list filter sheets and quick-view modals
Playwright a11y suite (axe) passes on /, /events, /restaurants, one detail page; new keyboard-path test added
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Builds on the completed WCAG work in memory (landmarks, touch targets done). Evidence: SearchAutocomplete lacks arrow-key handling; SocialEventCard/RestaurantCard action labels inconsistent.

userStories.title: Centralize category/cuisine colors into theme tokens (dark-mode complete)
userStories.description: As a user in dark mode, I need consistent, readable category colors; as a developer, one source of truth instead of per-component hardcoded gradients.
acceptanceCriteria: A single CATEGORY_STYLES map (or CSS custom properties) replaces hardcoded gradient/color literals in RestaurantCard (~47-64), SocialEventCard (~52-59), and any sibling components found by grep
Every token defines light + dark values; contrast >= 4.5:1 for text-bearing badges in both modes
Visual-regression spec updated/passes for card surfaces
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Web twin of IOS-POLISH-006. Low risk, high consistency payoff.

userStories.title: Contextual paywall modal with per-feature copy (web parity with iOS)
userStories.description: As the business, I need the web paywall to appear at the moment of feature desire with tailored copy — iOS ships PaywallView with 8 contexts and measurable per-surface conversion; web shows a generic gate.
acceptanceCriteria: Reusable PaywallModal accepting a context (id, headline, benefit bullets, recommended tier) with contexts mirroring iOS: unlimited favorites, trip planner, saved searches, custom alerts, advanced filters, ad-free, insider/dining tips
PremiumGate and feature-gate call sites present the contextual modal instead of generic copy/redirect to /pricing; checkout proceeds via the existing Stripe flow
Favorites cap (3 free) enforced on web with the unlimited-favorites context on the 4th save attempt
Every present/dismiss/checkout-start event logged with context id (existing analytics path) for per-surface conversion measurement
Modal is accessible (focus trap, Escape, focus restore) and mobile-friendly
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Mirror iOS IOS-SUB-010/011 (see archived notes in scripts/ralph/archive and git history for the context list + tier mapping). PremiumFeature keys should match the web useSubscription hasFeature() list to stay cross-platform consistent.

userStories.title: Annual plans + free trial on web (Stripe)
userStories.description: As a user, I want a cheaper annual option and a low-risk trial on web — iOS already sells Insider $49.99/yr and VIP $129.99/yr with a 7-day trial; web only offers monthly.
acceptanceCriteria: Pricing page and PaywallModal show a monthly/annual toggle with computed 'Save N%' badge (Insider $49.99/yr, VIP $129.99/yr to match iOS)
Checkout session supports the annual price IDs; scripts/setup-stripe-products.js extended to create them idempotently (document the one-time run in notes as ACTION REQUIRED if env keys absent)
7-day trial configured via Stripe trial_period_days for first-time subscribers; subscription status UI shows trial state and renewal date; legally-required renewal copy present
stripe-webhook handles trialing→active transitions; user_subscriptions tier resolves correctly during trial (matches the cross-platform resolution iOS relies on)
Tier parity preserved: web annual subscribers sync to mobile via the existing user_subscriptions mechanism
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Matches iOS IOS-SUB-012 economics. Touches money — keep changes additive and verify webhook idempotency. Flag any Stripe-dashboard manual steps as ACTION REQUIRED in progress notes.

userStories.title: Saved searches + alerts with automated nightly digest (promised, unbuilt)
userStories.description: As an Insider subscriber, I was promised 'saved searches & event alerts' on the pricing page, but the web has no way to save a search or receive alerts — a broken product promise and a retention loop left on the table.
acceptanceCriteria: Search/list pages get a 'Save this search' affordance (free users see the contextual paywall via WEB-FEAT-001; Insider 10 / VIP unlimited limits enforced server-side)
Dashboard tab lists saved searches with an alerts on/off toggle and delete; saved_searches table additive with RLS owner-only

Nightly job (WEB-AUTO-001 jobRunner): runs active saved searches against events created since last run, groups per user, sends ONE consolidated email via existing email plumbing with deep links back to the filtered URL (WEB-UX-001 URL-state makes the links possible)
Email respects unsubscribe/notification preferences; zero matches = no email
Per-tier limits and alert behavior logged for funnel analysis
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Depends on WEB-UX-001 (URL filter state for deep links) and pairs with WEB-FEAT-001 gating. iOS PARITY-008 defines the cross-platform shape — keep table/RPC design compatible so the native app can adopt it.

userStories.title: First-party campaign ad serving on web with house-ad fill
userStories.description: As an advertiser, my paid campaign should render on the web (it already renders on iOS); as the business, unsold inventory should sell subscriptions instead of showing nothing.
acceptanceCriteria: Web AdBanner fetches creatives via the existing get_active_ads(placement_type) RPC (same source as iOS CampaignAdService) for top_banner / below_fold / featured_spot placements, cached ~5min
Fallback chain campaign → affiliate → house ad (rotating 3 messages, CTA opens contextual paywall/pricing) so a slot never renders empty; FTC 'Ad' label on everything; Insider/VIP see zero ads
Impression/click tracking writes to the same ad_impressions/ad_clicks tables as iOS with viewability rules matching src/lib/tracking.ts thresholds (>=50% visible >=1s, deduped per session)
House vs paid vs affiliate distinguished in tracking payloads so fill rate is measurable
Lazy-loaded below the fold (no LCP regression — coordinate with WEB-PERF-003)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Web twin of IOS-ADS-010/013/014 — the RPC, tables, and thresholds all exist; web just never consumed them (current AdBanner shows one hardcoded affiliate creative).

userStories.title: Sponsored/featured listings inline in web browse lists
userStories.description: As an advertiser, my sponsored listing should be visibly boosted in web browse flows like it is in the iOS rails — clearly labeled, never disguised.
acceptanceCriteria: Events/Restaurants/Attractions list queries surface is_sponsored items at the top positions (cap 2) with an amber ring + 'Sponsored' badge matching the iOS treatment; organic order otherwise untouched
Sponsored impressions/clicks tracked distinctly (sponsored_listing inventory class) via the shared tracking lib
Shown to all tiers (content, not interruptive ads); VoiceOver/screen-reader text prefixes 'Sponsored'
Expired sponsorships (sponsored_until past) automatically lose the treatment with no manual cleanup
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Web twin of IOS-ADS-011; events/restaurants rows already carry is_sponsored/sponsored_until.

userStories.title: Guest favorites with signup migration (kill the save-wall)
userStories.description: As an anonymous visitor, I want to save a few favorites before being asked to sign up; as the business, visitors who invest first convert dramatically better than those hitting an auth wall.
acceptanceCriteria: Unauthenticated users can favorite up to 3 items, stored via @/lib/safeStorage (never raw localStorage), surviving reloads
Guest cap reached → contextual signup prompt ('Sign up free to keep saving') — not the paywall; favorites UI shows guest count (1/3)
On signup/login, guest favorites migrate to the user's server favorites automatically (idempotent, deduped) and the local copy clears
Dashboard/welcome surface acknowledges the migrated favorites
Conversion events logged (guest-save, wall-hit, signup-from-wall) for funnel measurement
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Highest-leverage funnel fix from the features audit. Keep the safeStorage schema versioned per CLAUDE.md on-disk-state rules.

userStories.title: Recently-viewed rail + personalized home section ordering
userStories.description: As a returning user, the homepage should reflect what I actually do here — quick resume of recently-viewed items and section ordering driven by my engagement, not a fixed layout.
acceptanceCriteria: Detail-page views record {id, type, timestamp} (signed-in: server table with RLS; guest: safeStorage), capped at 20, pruned > 30 days
Homepage gains a 'Recently viewed' rail (appears only when >= 3 entries); Dashboard gets the full list with remove
Home sections render from a data-driven order: users with dominant restaurant engagement see dining-first, etc.; guests/no-signal users keep the canonical order (deterministic, no layout flicker)
Personalized-cohort flag logged so conversion vs control is measurable
No CLS from personalization (order computed before first paint of the section list)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Web twin of iOS ForYou/IA-006 ordering. Index.tsx already renders ForYouRail + PersonalizedRecommendations — this story makes placement itself data-driven.

userStories.title: Dynamic OG-image generation for social shares
userStories.description: As the business, shared event/restaurant links should render rich branded preview cards (title, date, image) instead of a generic site image — direct social CTR lift with zero ongoing admin work.
acceptanceCriteria: Edge function og-image/:type/:id renders a branded PNG (Satori or canvas: gradient background, truncated title, date/rating badge, thumbnail) for events/restaurants/attractions/articles
Detail pages' og:image meta points at the function URL; prerender (scripts/prerender.mjs) emits the correct tags for crawler-visible HTML
Responses cached aggressively (immutable for past events, ~1h for upcoming); function rate-limited per WEB-SEC patterns
Validated with Twitter/Facebook preview debuggers (record screenshots in PR/progress notes)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Self-running marketing infrastructure — fits the autonomy theme. Check how prerender.mjs currently writes meta tags before wiring.

userStories.title: Map-first discovery: bounds-aware filtering on DiscoverMap
userStories.description: As a high-intent user, I want to pan the map and see what's in view — the existing DiscoverMap renders markers but supports no spatial interaction.
acceptanceCriteria: Map moveend captures bounds; a bounds query (RPC or lat/lng range filters) returns counts + items for events/restaurants/attractions in view
Sidebar/sheet lists in-view results as cards with a live count; layer toggles show/hide each content type's markers
'Search this area' button refreshes results for the current bounds; selected marker highlights its card and vice-versa
Mobile: bottom-sheet pattern, map remains usable; Leaflet stays lazy-loaded (WEB-PERF-003)
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Existing DiscoverMap page is the shell; content tables have lat/lng maintained by geocoding triggers (and WEB-AUTO-003 heals gaps).

userStories.title: Review composer with photo upload, wired through auto-moderation
userStories.description: As a user, I want to write a rating + review with photos on web; as the owner, all of it flows through the WEB-AUTO-009 moderation pipeline so UGC scales with zero manual review of the clean majority.
acceptanceCriteria: ReviewComposer (star picker, text, up to 3 photos) on Event/Restaurant/Attraction detail pages; auth-gated with a sign-in prompt for guests
Photos client-resized (< 500KB), uploaded to Supabase Storage with owner-scoped paths/RLS, URLs stored additively on the review row
Submissions route through moderate-content (WEB-AUTO-009): clean publishes instantly, flagged goes to the queue — user sees 'pending review' state honestly
Reviews render with author, relative date, stars, text, photo grid (lightbox); owners can edit/delete their own; report button feeds the moderation queue
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Sequenced after WEB-AUTO-009. RatingSystem + PremiumGate(writeReviews) components exist as the starting seam.

userStories.title: Trip Planner web polish: quota meter, contextual paywall, share, reorder, calendar
userStories.description: As a user, the web Trip Planner should match the native experience: today the form works but lacks the quota meter, contextual upsell, itinerary reorder, share link, and calendar export that iOS ships.
acceptanceCriteria: Quota meter shows tier usage (Insider 5/mo, VIP unlimited; free sees the trip-planner contextual paywall via WEB-FEAT-001) enforced against the same server-side counts as iOS
Itinerary view: day-by-day sections with reorder (drag or up/down) persisted via the existing trip_plans backend; map preview of stops (lazy Leaflet)
Share generates the public /trips/shared/<code> link with copy + native share; AddToCalendar exports per-day or whole-trip .ics plus Google Calendar deep-link
Loading/error/generation-failure states handled with the WEB-UX-002 patterns
npm run validate passes
userStories.notes: Backend (generate-itinerary, trip_plans, share codes, get_trip_itinerary RPC) all exists from the iOS build — this is pure web UI adoption. src/hooks/useTripPlanner.ts is the seam.
